findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed unsealed wood paneling on the walls next to the soda machine. Informed PIC that materials for floors, walls, and ceilings must be nonabsorbent to prevent contamination. Please either seal the wood with paint or replace the wood paneling with a smooth, cleanable, nonabsorbent material by the next routine inspection. Ensure that materials for interior floors, walls, and ceilings are nonabsorbent.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed the area in the back of the soda machines has several areas where there is a build up of moisture and soil residues, and the area cannot easily cleaned by staff as the equipment is bolted to the floor. There is a concern for mold. Inspector will Follow Up to make sure the area behind the soda machines is cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed that PIC does not currently have a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificate. No staff have a CFPM certificate. Medium Risk establishments must have a CFPM present when food preparation is occurring. Inspector will return for a Spot Check to confirm a CFPM is present during food preparation. Ensure the PIC is a CFPM.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed staff putting on gloves when switching tasks without washing their hands. CORRECTED: Staff washed their hands before putting on food safe gloves. Ensure that staff thoroughly clean hands between tasks that could cause cross-contamination, and especially before putting on food gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed that the handwashing sink was out of paper towels. CORRECTED: Paper towels were located and placed near the handwashing sink. PIC later refilled the paper towel dispenser during the inspection. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are provided with disposable towels that are used to both dry hands and act as a barrier between clean hands and the sink handles.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed several pieces of equipment in need of cleaning:
(i) The hood above the fryers and pizza oven has a significant buildup of grease and soil residues in the vent, which can contaminate food and is a potential fire hazard. The vent is also missing a protective screen to prevent residues from dripping onto prepared food. Staff do not recall when the hood was last cleaned. The hood MUST be cleaned PROFESSIONALLY, and cleaned at a frequency to prevent the build up of soil residues. Inspector will Follow Up to confirm the hood is cleaned.
(ii) The area in the back of the soda machines has a build up of moisture and soil residues in several areas. There is a concern for mold. The area cannot easily cleaned by staff (equipment is bolted to the floor). Inspector will Follow Up to confirm the area is cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(i) Observed that the sanitizer bucket (quaternary ammonium) was measured at concentrations too low for effective sanitizing (50ppm). CORRECTED: PIC refilled the bucket from the triple sink, and the sanitizer bucket was tested at an effective concentration of 200pm. Ensure that all sanitizing solutions are tested frequently to confirm effective sanitizing strength (200-400ppm for quat). Testing frequently also confirms if the triple sink is effectively sanitizing.
(ii) Observed that the kitchen area does not have a sanitizer bucket available; the main sanitizer bucket is in the front of the store. CORRECTED: PIC made a new separate sanitizer bucket for the kitchen. Ensure that a sanitizer bucket is available where food prep is happening.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed several nonfood-contact surfaces in need of more frequent cleaning:
(i) The drip tray of the soda dispensers had a significant buildup of soil residues. CORRECTED: During inspection, staff cleaned the residues in the drip tray and will prevent future buildup by cleaning the drip trays with more frequency.
(ii) The floor in several areas in the kitchen and the walk-ins has an accumulation of debris and soils.
(iii) The coffee makers have an accumulation of residues at the top.
Please clean these areas by the next routine inspection. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed several mops stored incorrectly, preventing them from air-drying: (i) on the floor with no place to drain; (ii) in the water basin of a mop bucket instead of the upper basket; (iii) in the bottom of the mop sink instead of hanging above the mop sink. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and staff fixed all mop storage issues. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air-dry and drain without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the front portion of the left roller had ambient food temperatures of about 68-74F. Upon investigation the PIC noticed that the front portion was turned off. The back portion of the roller was turned on and had an ambient air temperature of about 150F. The PIC discarded the food on the front portion of the roller and turned on the roller during the inspection. When the roller was checked at the end of the inspection the ambient air was 180F. Ensure that temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Observed the pizzas at the front were not properly marked for time-as-control. When pizzas are brought from the back a sticker is placed above which indicates when the pizza was prepared and when it must be discarded. The pizzas currently on display did not have a sticker. The PIC and inspector discussed the importance of identifying the 4-hour window for time-as-control. The PIC voluntarily discarded the pizzas during the inspection. The newly made pizzas were properly marked with a sticker. Ensure when using time-as-control the time is marked to indicate when the 4-hour window has passed and food must be discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed several foods stored on the floor throughout the facility. The foods stored on the floor included: (1) Boxes of sliced banana peppers and various cans on the floor adjacent to the back hand sink; and (2) Boxes of food (including, but not limited too, creamer and pastries) stored on the floor of the walk-in cooler. Ensure that foods are stored at least 6-inches above the ground to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed a mop stored with the head in the mop sink basin. The PIC inverted the mop during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the facility attempted to fix the peeling cove base by stapling it to the wall, however, there are still gaps between the cove base and the wall. Specifically, the cove base that still has gaps is around the utility sink by the pizza prep station and the soda machine. The cove base needs to be more closely sealed to the wall. Either the facility needs to use more staples or they must use another technique. Ensure that all surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the following must be cleaned: (1) The accumulation of garage and food debris in the walk-in cooler underneath the back shelving; and (2) The large drink spillage by the soda machine lines. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Observed the whip cream in the whip cream dispenser at the coffee station was moldy. Before whip cream goes into dispenser it is being stored in the walk-in cooler. There is currently two large boxes in the walk-in cooler full of whip cream bags. The package states the bags can only be refrigerated for 2-weeks before being throw away. The PIC stated that they did not know when the delivery had come, but it was most likely well over 2-weeks ago. The package also stated that whip cream can only be stored at room temperature for 5 days. The whip cream had most likely been in the dispenser for longer than 5 days. The PIC removed the whip cream dispenser from service during the inspection. The boxes of whip cream in the walk-in cooler were also discarded during the inspection. Ensure that whip cream is being stored according to its requirements to keep it safe for consumption.

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed several TSC food items being maintained above 41F in two locations: (1) In the front area, the open cooler’s digital thermometer was reading 81F. The ambient air of the cooler was observed to be about 74F at the top and 45F at the bottom for the food on the outside. The food on the bottom shelf in the very back was temping at 41F or below and was moved to the walk-in cooler. However, the vast majority of the food in this cooler was discarded (including, but not limited too, cakes, puddings, cheese, and various deli meats). Food that does not need to be refrigerated was allowed to remain in the cooler. (2) In the walk-in cooler, the food by the entrance door to the cooler had an ambient reading of about 50F. The milk was probed to be 49F and was thrown away. There was also a variety of other foods (including, but not limited too, creamer, half & half, boiled eggs, sausage, ham, French toast, breakfast sandwiches, and any drinks that need to be refrigerated) which were also above 41F and were discarded. Cooked bacon and food that was still frozen from a delivery truck that just came were the only food not discarded. There was additional food that is stored at the back of the walk-in cooler by the freezer. The distance from the entrance door meant the food was temping at 41F or below, and therefore did not need to be discarded. The food from the delivery that was still frozen was moved to the back of the walk-in cooler

All of the above mentioned food which were temping at 41F or above were discarded during the inspection. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at 41F or below. For information about the coolers, see violation #33.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed that the following coolers were not cold holding food at 41F or below: (1) Open cooler in the front holding cheese, crackers, deli meats, and other snack items; and (2) The portion of the walk-in cooler next to the entrance door. All food above 41F were discarded (see violation #22). The high temperatures of the coolers could be impacted by the warm temperatures of the store. The inspector suggests getting service on the air conditioning. Ensure that equipment for cold holding is sufficient to provide food temperatures below 41F. The follow-up will conducted on 08/19/2024 to ensure that coolers are properly cold holding.

For information on discarded food, see violation #22.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of food being stored in the walk-in freezer on the floor. Food needs to be stored at least 6-inches of the ground to prevent cross contamination. Ensure that food is stored at least 6-inches off the floor at all times.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket in the pizza prep area when inspector arrived. The employee made a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that there is a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the selves holding clean dishes in the pizza prep area are soiled. Non-food contact surfaces need to be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink by the pizza prep area has a drip at the faucet. Ensure that plumbing systems are maintained in good repair. There will be a follow-up on 08/19/2024 to ensure that the leak at the hand sink has been repaired.

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed mops being stored with the head in the water of the bucket and with the heads on the floor. Mops need to be stored in a position that allows the head to air dry. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position where the head can air dry when not in use.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the following violation has not been corrected: Base coving throughout the facility is peeling badly. All areas subject to food/water at any time must be sealed to be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that base coving is repaired/replaced to create easily cleanable surfaces in all areas subject to food/water including but not limited to near the soda machine, ice bins in back (note: ice machines have been removed, so this specific location is unknown to the inspector), utility sink (by the pizza prep area), and any other areas where base coving has peeled/been damaged. (REPEAT)

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the following physical facilities need to be cleaned: (1) Adjacent to the pizza prep cooler on the left; (2) Around the back hand sink; and (3) Floors of the walk-in freezer. Ensure the physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a large amount of mold growth on the underside of the upper coffee machine head and coming from the drain pipe of the soda machine ice bins. The ice bins are not designed in a way that facilitates cleaning and cannot be opened easily be staff on site to clean or inspect regularly. The mold from the drain pipe indicates that there likely mold present within the bins themselves. A 10-day follow-up has been issued for 12/18/2/2023 to have the ice bins serviced/cleaned. Operator has been provided with contact information to send pictures of the interior of the bins during cleaning in-lieu of follow-up. During the inspection, the ice bin was opened up and appears to be generally clean. There is a minimal amount of growth in nonfood-contact areas of the ice bin. Operator has been instructed to thoroughly clean as much of the machine as possible with bleach to prevent further mold growth apparent at the end of the drain line. Ensure that food-contact surfaces remain cleaned and sanitized at all times. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The area around the soda machine is heavily soiled with residue and debris. A thorough deep cleaning of this area is required. Ensure that all boxes of soda are removed and the area is opened up as much as possible to facilitate cleaning of this entire area. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Base coving throughout the facility is peeling badly. All areas subject to food/water at any time must be sealed to be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that base coving is repaired/replaced to create easily cleanable surfaces in all areas subject to food/water including but not limited to near the soda machine, ice bins in back, utility sink, and any other areas where base coving has peeled/been damaged.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
No hand soap was provided at the hand sink behind the front counter. Operator stated finished bottle and tossed today but it was not replaced. Hand soap was provided during the inspection. Corrected on site. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Whipped topping dispenser contained whipped topping without a date marking. The topping was discarded and replaced with a new one and date marked during the inspection. The product should be date marked for five days post-opening. Corrected on site. 

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Tongs were observed being stored on top of piles of single use items. Utensils must be stored in a clean and sanitized location to prevent contamination. The tongs were moved and hung properly. Corrected on site. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Dirty water was observed pooling underneath the rear of the soda machines. The water was cleaned up immediately. Corrected on site. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: See 6/24/21 routine inspection report for details

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the front counter handwashing sink. Handwashing sign was provided and posted. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Sanitizer solution at the 3 part sink was not adequate to provide proper sanitization of surfaces after washing and rinsing of equipment. Only the bottom edge of pizza trays were in contact with solution, and the basin used for sanitizing was only about a quarter full of solution. Employee doing dishes was advised on proper immersion and contact time during manual ware washing. Additional sanitizer solution was added to provide for proper immersion and contact time. 
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 30 seconds for quaternary ammonia chemical sanitizing solutions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Date mark was not present on open whipped topping in the dispenser at the drink counter. Product is good for 5 days at room temperature once opened for use. Store manager was unsure as to when product was opened. Product was discarded. A fresh bag of whipped topping was provided with a proper date mark.
Ensure a proper date mark is provided for in-use whipped topping and that product is used or discarded within 5 days once opened per manufacturer's instructions.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Bleach solution at front counter was observed with a concentration at +200ppm. Inspector's test strip began to bleach out and had some white spots. Effective concentration of 100-200ppm is listed on manufacturer's label. Solution was diluted to allow for proper concentration. 
Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 An infrared thermometer is the only food temperature measuring device available for use at the facility. Availability and use of stem thermometers were discussed. Obtain and use stem thermometers with a temperature registering range of 0°F-220°F to verify proper cooking, hot holding, and cold holding temperatures.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Chlorine test kit is not available for verifying concentration of bleach solution used to wipe down surfaces at food service counters.
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided. Provide a chlorine test kit for checking bleach solutions.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430  Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. At least one employee has an expired food handler certification. Ensure all staff without food manager certifications have current food handler certifications. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
